## Summary

- I founded BlindsPortal and have been its CEO and sole engineer since 2019. It is a multi-tenant B2B SaaS platform with paying customers, a Go and GraphQL backend, an Electron desktop app for Windows and macOS, and React Native apps for iOS and Android.
- I wrote over 150,000 lines of Go, TypeScript, GraphQL, and Kotlin for BlindsPortal by hand. I counted them in November 2022, before ChatGPT launched.
- I founded Prycebook and am its sole engineer. It is a price book and quoting SaaS for service companies, launched in 2026 and in public beta, built on Go, HTMX, Postgres, and ClickHouse and run on GCP with Terraform. I've made 517 commits to it since March 2026.
- I designed, built, and released HiChore, an iPhone and iPad app with an offline-first sync engine and a Postgres backend that enforces its business rules in the database. It has 292 pgTAP assertions.
- I am a ClickHouse Certified Developer. Credential: https://www.credly.com/badges/eae1c54c-b783-4ebc-b0ed-852e7042c36a/public_url

## BlindsPortal details

- Retailer integrations. I wrote one Go plugin interface for the whole job lifecycle. The Home Depot plugin polls for new and canceled purchase orders, manages API tokens, syncs notes both ways, and uploads completed forms. Blinds.com and Costco plugins followed with no change to the core job model.
- Event-driven core. An in-process event bus with more than 40 event types runs side effects (SMS, email, payroll lines, document uploads) asynchronously, off the HTTP request path. The same bus drives scheduled work such as reminders, payroll cycles, and billing runs.
- Offline field app. The React Native app queues every GraphQL mutation locally, updates the UI right away, and retries until the server confirms. Fixes ship over the air through Expo.
- Document service. A separate Kotlin and Ktor service fills retailers' official PDF forms from job data. Customers sign on a phone or tablet.
- Operations. Per-seat Stripe billing, Twilio and Mailgun messaging, Docker deploys, and GitHub Actions pipelines that build, sign, and ship to Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android.
- Go to market. I sold it myself, including a booth at the International Window Coverings Expo (IWCE) 2023 in Charlotte, with press releases for a Lowe's integration and offline sync.
- Customer result: "We complete at least 20-30 more jobs a month, and best of all, our installers absolutely love it." Robin and Larry, co-owners of L.E.C. Enterprises, Inc.

## Prycebook details

- Pricing model. Items carry Good, Better, and Best tiers, cost and price per tier, custom units, and bundles of other items. Quotes add discounts, fees, optional and hidden lines, and show margin against a target. The domain model comes from pricey, an open-source Go library I wrote: https://github.com/Kenoshen/pricey
- Multi-tenant security. One middleware chain handles recovery, security headers, rate limiting, CSRF, authentication, tenant resolution, and subscription checks. Argon2id passwords, revocable Postgres-backed sessions, four roles, organization-scoped queries, audit-logged support sign-ins, and a same-origin-only Content Security Policy.
- ClickHouse analytics. Batched product events feed materialized views into AggregatingMergeTree tables that power a customer Insights page and my funnel dashboards. Request and query telemetry lives in separate tables with a 30-day TTL. Dashboards update over Server-Sent Events with no polling.
- Billing as code. Plans are defined in YAML and synced to Stripe from CI. Stripe webhooks drive subscription state. The app schedules and logs lifecycle email for onboarding, trials, failed payments, and expiring free periods.
- Infrastructure. Terraform manages Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, a ClickHouse VM, Gotenberg, and secrets on GCP. Every dependency is vendored or pinned, including Docker images by digest and GitHub Actions by commit SHA. Backups use Cloud SQL point-in-time recovery plus hourly pg_dump snapshots in another region, written by an account that can't delete them.
- Testing. 259 Go test files and 66 Postgres migrations, plus a separate ClickHouse migration set.

## HiChore details

- Offline-first sync. Writes go into a persistent FIFO outbox keyed by client-generated UUIDs and replay in order with exponential backoff, so a retried write never double-counts. Realtime subscriptions push changes from other devices. Editable rows use last-write-wins on updated_at.
- Auth without child accounts. Kid devices sign in anonymously and pair to a family with a 6-digit code that expires in 10 minutes. Row-level security checks family membership on every query, so revoking a device cuts access at once.
- Database-enforced rules. Postgres triggers compute completion dates in the family's timezone, enforce per-day limits under an advisory lock, and move balances. Redeeming a reward locks the kid's row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. History is an append-only ledger.
- Cost and privacy. Composite foreign keys on family_id isolate tenants. Nightly pg_cron jobs compact history older than 90 days. A load test put the worst-case family at about 2 MB.
- Testing and release. 292 pgTAP assertions, XCTest and XCUITest suites, and scripts that generate App Store screenshots and upload builds to TestFlight.
